title: Corner Gradient Descent
claim: Achievable acceleration depends on problem spectral exponents, with distinct regimes separated by sharp boundaries in a two-parameter phase diagram.
layout: 2 side-by-side phase diagrams sharing axes, left-to-right, colorbar on right
description: Two phase diagrams share the same axes: zeta on the horizontal axis and 1/nu on the vertical axis. The left panel has flat colored bands. A magenta band at the top is labeled immediate divergence. A pink band below it is labeled eventual divergence. The bottom band splits diagonally into a green signal-dominated region and a yellow noise-dominated region. Each region has its loss-rate formula, and two blue stars mark CIFAR10+ResNet and MNIST+MLP in the green region. The right panel is a heatmap with a rainbow gradient from blue to red, plus a colorbar for theta_max running from 1 to 2. Dashed black lines split it into regions I, II and III, and each region is labeled with its theta_max formula. The eye goes first to the saturated red and magenta areas.
caption: Left: The phase diagram of stationary finite-memory SGD from Velikanov et al. (2023); Yarotsky & Velikanov (2024). Right: Maximum acceleration factor θmax = min(2, ν, 2 ζ+1/ν ) for Corner SGD in the signal-dominated regime (see Theorem 4).
abstract: We consider SGD-type optimization on infinite-dimensional quadratic problems with power law spectral conditions. It is well-known that on such problems deterministic GD has loss convergence rates $L_t=O(t^{-Î¶})$, which can be improved to $L_t=O(t^{-2Î¶})$ by using Heavy Ball with a non-stationary Jacobi-based schedule (and the latter rate is optimal among fixed schedules). However, in the mini-batch Stochastic GD setting, the sampling noise causes the Jacobi HB to diverge; accordingly no $O(t^{-2Î¶})$ algorithm is known. In this paper we show that rates up to $O(t^{-2Î¶})$ can be achieved by a generalized stationary SGD with infinite memory. We start by identifying generalized (S)GD algorithms with contours in the complex plane. We then show that contours that have a corner with external angle $Î¸Ï$ accelerate the plain GD rate $O(t^{-Î¶})$ to $O(t^{-Î¸Î¶})$. For deterministic GD, increasing $Î¸$ allows to achieve rates arbitrarily close to $O(t^{-2Î¶})$. However, in Stochastic GD, increasing $Î¸$ also amplifies the sampling noise, so in general $Î¸$ needs to be optimized by balancing the acceleration and noise effects. We prove that the optimal rate is given by $Î¸_{\max}=\min(2,Î½,\tfrac{2}{Î¶+1/Î½})$, where $Î½,Î¶$ are the exponents appearing in the capacity and source spectral conditions. Furthermore, using fast rational approximations of the power functions, we show that ideal corner algorithms can be efficiently approximated by finite-memory algorithms, and demonstrate their practical efficiency on a synthetic problem and MNIST.
